name: Kuntz HoLEP versus open prostatectomy
question: How do holmium laser enucleation and transvesical open prostatectomy compare in obstructed men with prostates larger than 100 g?

arms.label: Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate

design.population: 120 men with symptomatic, urodynamically confirmed obstruction, AUA symptom score at least 8, peak flow at most 12 mL/s, postvoid residual greater than 50 mL, and prostate volume at least 100 mL on transrectal ultrasonography.
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, Patients, pp 1465–1466; Table 1, p 1466

verdictNote: No primary endpoint or equivalence margin was specified; six-month outcomes included 104 completers.
takeaway: In 120 men with obstructed prostates at least 100 mL, HoLEP and transvesical open prostatectomy improved six-month voiding measures without significant between-arm differences among 104 completers. HoLEP required longer surgery but reduced hemoglobin loss, catheter time, hospital stay and transfusions.

reports.label: Six-month primary report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation, October 2002; day not reported
reports.citation: Kuntz RM, Lehrich K. "Transurethral holmium laser enucleation versus transvesical open enucleation for prostate adenoma greater than 100 gm.: a randomized prospective trial of 120 patients." *J Urol.* 2002;168(4 Pt 1):1465-1469. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(05)64475-8
reports.followUp: Assessments at 1, 3 and 6 months; 104/120 completed six months (54/60 HoLEP, 50/60 open) after 7 losses to follow-up and exclusion of 9 incidental prostate cancers
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1466; Results, Patient population, p 1466; Table 3, p 1467

results.note: Between-arm Mann–Whitney comparison; within-arm improvement P<0.0001. No primary endpoint, effect estimate, confidence interval or equivalence margin specified.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3, p 1467; Materials and Methods, p 1466

results.measure: Mean Qmax at six months among 104 completers
results.note: Between-arm Mann–Whitney comparison; within-arm improvement P<0.0001. The printed open-arm six-month SD appears inconsistent with its range; mean alone recorded.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3, p 1467; Materials and Methods, p 1466

results.note: Between-arm Mann–Whitney comparison; within-arm improvement P<0.0001.

harms.label: Blood transfusion
harms.note: P=0.003; all transfusions were clinically indicated for hemodynamic compromise or hemoglobin below 7 g/dL.

harms.label: Reoperation through six months
harms.note: P=0.75; arterial bleeding 3/60 in each arm, secondary apical resection 2/60 versus 0/60, bladder-neck contracture 0/60 versus 2/60, urethral stricture 1/60 versus 0/60.

harms.label: Persistent mild stress incontinence at three months
harms.note: Eleven initially continent patients had postoperative moderate-to-severe incontinence (5 HoLEP, 6 open); all but two HoLEP patients resolved by three months.

delivery.label: Operative and recovery comparisons

values.exp: Mean operation 135.9 ± 31.2 min; hemoglobin loss 1.9 ± 1.3 g/dL; catheter 30.8 ± 17.3 h; hospital stay 69.6 ± 36.4 h
values.ctl: Mean operation 90.6 ± 19.5 min; hemoglobin loss 2.8 ± 1.6 g/dL; catheter 194.4 ± 20.1 h; hospital stay 251.0 ± 45.5 h

delivery.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 1467; Materials and Methods, Holmium laser enucleation, p 1466
delivery.note: Each comparison P<0.0001. HoLEP used 80 or 100 W (2.0 J at 40 or 50 Hz), retrograde enucleation from apex to bladder; lobes retrieved by loop fragmentation (50/60) or mechanical morcellation (10/60).
